input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: The only licence grant to us is § 4(c) (p0021). It is royalty-free, non-exclusive and perpetual, is not labelled revocable or terminable at the Contractor's discretion, and nothing in § 6 (Termination) revokes it on termination — so the walk-away risk (licence revocable at Vendor's discretion) is absent. Affiliates and contractors are not named, but the express "right to grant a sublicense" for use "in connection with Company's business operations" gives us a clear path to extend the licence to affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, which meets or exceeds the fallback's "affiliates covered on written notice". Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: the grant does not say "irrevocable" expressly (perpetuity plus the absence of any revocation trigger achieves substantially the same result), and successor transfer is governed by the general non-assignment clause in p0042, which requires consent that "will not be unreasonably withheld" — a workable route to a successor in an M&A transaction. The clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and we would not redline it; if the Contractor reopens § 4, we would take the opportunity to add "irrevocable", name affiliates and contractors, and carve M&A successors out of the assignment consent.
